newsitem.title: UK: UK construction set for little growth ahead - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK construction set for little growth ahead - survey.

text.p: The UK construction industry is unlikely to see notable real growth over the next five years and continues to underperform the industrial average for return on capital, according to a survey published on Wednesday.

The COBA Group consultancy said the industry was likely to remain in the doldrums. The survey is based on comments from senior decision-makers in the UK's biggest construction and building materials companies.
On return on capital, the survey said the building material sector's average was 10 percent, with construction at 11 percent and the industry average at 13 percent.

The positive benefits of National Lottery cash on new projects plus Private Finance Initiative spending has been outweighed by severe cutbacks in government expenditure on infrastructure, particularly on roads.
The companies have little hope of an improvement in funding if the opposition Labour Party wins the next election due by May 1997.
Only one third predict faster growth as a result.

Oliver Walker of The COBA Group said the industry would have to do four things to achieve profitable growth -- consolidate, rationalise to increase efficiency, expand internationally based on existing products or services and cut costs.
"Businesses that fail to adopt a clear business strategy to achieve these goals will fail," he warned.
